internal.title: Incident Report: Elevated Error Rate in Checkout Service Due to Payment Service Flag
internal.body:
At 12:36 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Diagnosis identified that the root cause was an error injection in the payment service caused by the 'paymentFailure' flag. This flag caused a significant increase in payment errors and latency, impacting the checkout process.

The remediation involved disabling the 'paymentFailure' flag at 12:55 UTC after approval. Post-remediation monitoring confirmed recovery with error rates returning to normal levels.

Key timeline:
- 12:36:01: Alert received for high error rate in checkout
- 12:55:44: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection
- 12:55:54: Flag disabled after approval
- 12:55:54: Recovery verified

No other services were found to be contributing factors. The frontend service's error injection hypothesis was refuted.

Severity: SEV2

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing errors
external.body: Between 12:36 and 12:56 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced issues completing checkout due to payment processing errors. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a problematic payment processing feature. Normal service was restored promptly, and customers should no longer experience checkout failures.

lessons.lesson: Ensure that error injection flags are carefully controlled and monitored to prevent unintended service disruptions.
lessons.applies_when: When error injection flags like 'paymentFailure' are enabled in the payment service.

action_items: Review and improve flag management processes to prevent accidental enabling of disruptive flags.
Enhance monitoring to detect and alert on error injection flags being enabled in production environments.
